subject: Finex evaluation: vendor comparison summary + proposed smoke tests
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jeni Alvarez <jeni.alvarez@finexhealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today

Hi Jeni — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap while it's fresh and to align on next steps.

Key pain you described:
- High per-token costs and unpredictable tail latency on peak billing cycles (especially for episodic batch workloads).
- Difficulty getting consistent inference performance across cloud and on-prem for regulated workflows.
- Need for clear auditability (per-request logs + key rotation) and an SLA for sustained throughput.

Goals you shared:
- Reduce unit inference cost by ~30% while keeping 95th pct latency < 300ms for 512-token requests.
- Run a 2-week bakeoff to validate throughput and parity vs current provider.
- Confirm security controls for SOC2 + customer-managed KMS.

Competitive context you mentioned: evaluating NebulaAI and CloudPrompt alongside Redwood.

Proposed next steps (happy to adjust):
1) We’ll prepare a short smoke-test plan that mirrors your production mix and share it by EOD Monday (Camila will own).
2) You provide a small sample workload + expected SLO targets and a security contact for questionnaire follow-up (Rahul?).
3) Schedule a 90-minute lab session week of 11/23 to run live parity tests and throughput ramps.

Attachments: I’ll attach the proposed smoke-test template + a light competitor checklist for context.

If that aligns, we’ll kick off the lab and Camila will coordinate exact test vectors.

Thanks — Sean

From: Jeni Alvarez <jeni.alvarez@finexhealth.com>

Cc: Rahul Patel <rahul.patel@finexhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today

Sean — good summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: we do want to replicate two request patterns — interactive triage (median ~80 tokens, bursty) and nightly cohort scoring (avg 420 tokens, high throughput). Our current provider meets cost targets for batch runs but struggles on interactive bursts which affect our clinician UX.

On security: Rahul is correct contact for SOC2/KMS — he’ll send over our standard supplier questionnaire; if you can point us to the audit artifacts we normally need (SOC2 Type II report + KMS integration notes), that’d be helpful.

About competitors: NebulaAI’s price/latency numbers look attractive for batch, and CloudPrompt sells stronger regional presence (APAC) — both have tradeoffs on tooling/observability. We want the bakeoff focused on the two SLOs above and one basic fidelity check (extraction accuracy on our annotation set).

We’ll share a 48-hour sample workload extract by EOD Tuesday. Lab week of 11/23 works for a 90-min live run — prefer 11/24 afternoon PT.

— Jeni

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jeni Alvarez <jeni.alvarez@finexhealth.com>, Rahul Patel <rahul.patel@finexhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Smoke-test plan + decision criteria (draft)

Hi Jeni / Rahul — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a first-pass smoke-test plan and a lightweight competitor comparison note (high level). Highlights below so you don’t have to open the sheet immediately: 

Planned smoke tests (short):
- Interactive burst: 1k concurrent short sessions (80 tokens) for 10m window — measure 95th pct latency, p99 CPU/GPU utilization.
- Batch cohort scoring: 100k requests @ 420 tokens in ramped batches — measure throughput (tokens/s), cost per 1k tokens, and error rate.
- Fidelity spot-check: run 500 examples from your annotated set against our best open model and your current baseline, report extraction F1.

Decision criteria (suggested):
- Latency SLO: 95th < 300ms on interactive burst test (must pass).
- Cost target: <= 0.7x current provider for batch cost (preferred).
- Observability/security: per-request logs and offer for SOC2 + KMS integration docs (must pass).

Open questions for your team:
1) Will the sample workload include user-identifiers (PII)? If yes we’ll provide handling guidance and we’ll need a signed DPA for test data.
2) Are you open to running our cache-enabled profile during batch runs (it reduces unit cost but changes cold-start behavior)?

Next action: Marissa will propose 3x 90-min slots for 11/24-11/25 and create a calendar invite that captures required SRE/infra participants.

Attachments included: finex-smoke-test-plan.xlsx, competitor-comparison-notes.pdf

Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
